newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Maradona's manager surrenders after day on run.
newsitem.headline: Maradona's manager surrenders after day on run.

text.p: After spending most of Wednesday on the run, soccer star Diego Maradona's manager Guillermo Coppola turned himself in to Argentine police who suspect him of drug trafficking.

Police said Coppola surrendered to the authorities near his Buenos Aires luxury apartment, where an early-morning police raid had found more than one pound (500 grams) of cocaine in a large flower vase filled with sand.
Coppola had proclaimed his innocence in a telephone call from a secret hiding place to a local television station a few hours before giving himself up. Sounding nervous, he said he had been framed.
"What they found was not mine, someone put it there," he said, avoiding an interviewer's question of where he was.

"I feel calm, with my conscience clear. I'm going to present myself to the courts as is due, as I have always done in all the cases I've been involved in," Coppola said. He said he had not been at his apartment for several days but had left keys with the doorman to let police in in case they raided.

Coppola denied Argentine media reports of a bugged telephone conversation with Maradona in the power of investigators in which he allegedly offered the player pills to eliminate evidence of cocaine in post-match drug tests.
"I don't believe such a tape could exist."
Coppola said he was prepared to undergo tests for drug use himself, as long as they were carried out in public.
Judge Hernan Bernasconi ordered the arrest of Coppola after the find and said he had informed Interpol.
"In the police raid we found half a kilo(gram) of cocaine and some tablets, which we still can't determine if they're drugs," Bernasconi told reporters.
The judge said the arrest was ordered on grounds of "possession of drugs for commercial purposes."
Bernasconi has ordered several drug raids in recent days, arresting Maradona's brother-in-law Gabriel Esposito and former Argentine national team player Alberto Tarantini.

"It surprised us (to find cocaine), but the procedure is indisputable because the raid was carried out in the presence of witnesses and Mr. Coppola's lawyers," Bernasconi said. He said he had no evidence against Maradona.
Separately, police commissioner Emilio Azzaro said Coppola's apartment has been watched since March.
